title: APC Switched Rack PDU Phase Load Imbalance
exclusions: Does not replace enterprise SIEM correlation for unrelated threat classes. Pair with sibling UCs in the same subcategory when the SPL surface alone cannot prove control effectiveness (see prerequisiteUseCases on UC-15.1.30).

dataSources: PowerNet-MIB `rPDULoadStatusLoad` / per-phase load columns on `sourcetype=snmp:apc:pdu` (three-phase rPDU models) Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase #1537), Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase #6266) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=power sourcetype=snmp:apc:pdu host=*
| eval p1=tonumber(rPDULoadStatusLoad1), p2=tonumber(rPDULoadStatusLoad2), p3=tonumber(rPDULoadStatusLoad3)
| eval maxp=max(p1,p2,p3), minp=min(min(p1,p2),p3)
| eval imbalance=round(maxp-minp,1)
| where imbalance > 20 AND isnotnull(p1)
| table _time, host, pdu_name, p1, p2, p3, imbalance
| sort - imbalance
description: Three-phase rack PDUs suffer neutral current and breaker stress when one leg is overloaded. Comparing `rPDULoadStatusLoad1..3` exposes uneven IT load distribution across phases before overheating or upstream breaker trips.
value: Improves electrical safety and utilization by guiding rack cord routing and PDU balancing using SNMP already collected for outlet UC-15.1.7.
implementation: Field names vary by MIB branch (`rPDULoadStatusLoad` table indices). Use `snmpwalk` to confirm exact suffixes and map to `rPDULoadStatusLoad1` fields in `props.conf`. Single-phase PDUs will null out—filter with `isnotnull(p1)`. Tune imbalance >20% (of max phase rating) per facility engineering. Poll every 5 minutes.
visualization: Stacked bar (p1–p3), Table (worst imbalance), Heatmap (PDU × phase).
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance windows** — Planned change activity in the CMDB or change calendar produces expected deviations that match this detection pattern during approved maintenance. Cross-check ServiceNow change records for `state=implement` and the affected CI list.

2. **Backup and batch job cycles** — Nightly ETL, backup agents, or log rotation jobs generate bursts of similar events that resemble alert conditions but occur on a fixed schedule. Compare `_time` against the documented batch window before paging.

3. **Onboarding and provisioning bursts** — New users, devices, or services provisioned in bulk can temporarily skew counts until baselines stabilize. Filter events tagged `onboarding=true` in the identity or asset lookup.

4. **Monitoring and health-check traffic** — Synthetic transactions or internal scanner accounts generate probe traffic designed to exercise the control. Exclude service accounts listed in `monitoring_exceptions.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** Maintain a KV Store lookup `operational_exceptions.csv` with columns `entity`, `exception_reason`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, and `approved_by`. Join the saved search to this lookup and filter `where isnull(exception_reason) OR now() > valid_until` so approved windows suppress alerts without muting the search globally.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• DCIM with phase labeling per outlet strip.
• Electrician review of thresholds.

Step 1 — MIB walk on a reference rPDU.

Step 2 — Align extractions with UC-15.1.7 outlet metrics.

Step 3 — Change management for cord moves.

Step 4 — Optional Modbus path if SNMP disabled.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase #1537), Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase #6266) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=snmp:apc:pdu into power. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`imbalance`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
